record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Give a characterization of inﬁne words whose com- plexity satisﬁes limn p(n)/n = 2.

evidence.quote: Give a characterization of inﬁne words whose com- plexity satisﬁes limn p(n)/n = 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and let $w \in A^{\mathbb{N}}$ be an infinite word. For each integer $n \geq 0$, let $p_w(n)$ denote the factor complexity of $w$, i.e., the number of distinct factors (contiguous finite subwords) of $w$ of length $n$.

Provide a characterization (in terms of structural / combinatorial properties such as substitutive structure, return words, S-adic representations, or similar) of all infinite words $w$ that satisfy
$$\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{p_w(n)}{n} = 2.$$
That is, describe explicitly the class of infinite words whose factor complexity is asymptotically equivalent to $2n$.
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search on combinatorics on words turns up many partial results on linear factor complexity (e.g., Sturmian words with p(n) = n+1, Arnoux–Rauzy words, words coming from interval exchanges and S-adic systems, and general structure theorems for words with p(n) = O(n)), but no source provides a complete characterization of infinite words satisfying lim p(n)/n = 2. The status of a full characterization of this asymptotic class appears to remain open or at least not definitively settled in the available sources.

status_evidence.title: Infinite Words with very Low Factor Complexity
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on infinite words of low factor complexity, including Sturmian and Arnoux–Rauzy words, but no complete characterization of words with lim p(n)/n = 2.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys on low factor complexity do not provide a full characterization of words satisfying lim p(n)/n = 2.

status_evidence.title: Factor complexity (Cassaigne–Nicolas chapter)
status_evidence.snippet: Standard reference chapter on factor complexity discusses linear-complexity words and structural results, without giving a definitive characterization of the asymptotic class lim p(n)/n = 2.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references on factor complexity do not state a complete characterization of this asymptotic class.
